action: Close extra tabs, take three slow breaths, and write the next visible action before working for five minutes.

citations.excerpt: A brief pause followed by a defined next action can reduce restart friction.

claims.statement: A short reset can support a focused return.

citations.excerpt: Writing the next visible action removes a decision from the return to work.

claims.statement: A written next action reduces restart decisions.

depths.core: Attention recovery starts by reducing choice. Close what you do not need, pause, and define one visible action. Work on only that action for five minutes.
depths.deep: When attention feels scattered, trying to force a long focus session adds pressure. A short reset creates a clean boundary. Writing the next visible action removes the need to decide again when you return. Five minutes is enough to practice the return without asking for perfect concentration.
depths.quick: Reset, write one next action, and work on it for five minutes.

takeaway: Recover attention by making the return small and specific.
title: Return to one task
